# JVM: GraalVM native-image and the alternatives

**documented**, not measured: the probe host had a JRE but no GraalVM.

⭐ **Two genuinely different approaches**, and the distinction matters more here
than in any other ecosystem: compile the program to a native binary, or ship a
JVM alongside it.

---

## 1. Fully static: yes, with GraalVM native-image

```sh
native-image --static --libc=musl \
  --no-fallback \
  -H:+ReportExceptionStackTraces \
  -o out/app -jar app.jar
```

⭐ **`--static --libc=musl` produces a fully static binary with no
`PT_INTERP`.** It requires a musl toolchain and a static `zlib` present at
build time.

⛔ **`--no-fallback` is mandatory for a distributed package.** Without it,
native-image silently produces a *fallback image*: a launcher that requires a
full JVM at run time. It looks like it worked. It is not a static binary and it
fails on any machine without a JVM.

⚠ **That is the single most important trap in this ecosystem** and it is quiet:
the build succeeds, the binary runs on the build machine, and it fails for
users.

## 2. libc

| option | note |
| --- | --- |
| ⭐ `--libc=musl` with `--static` | ⭐ fully static |
| `--libc=glibc` with `--static` | ⚠ works, inherits glibc-static limits |
| ⭐ `--static-nolibc` | links everything but libc; smaller, still needs a host libc |
| dynamic, the default | not portable |

## 3. Compiler and toolchain

| | |
| --- | --- |
| GraalVM `native-image` | ⛔ pin the GraalVM version by image digest |
| a musl toolchain | required for `--libc=musl` |
| `zlib` static | required |

⚠ **GraalVM's build is memory-hungry**: several gigabytes for a
non-trivial application. `[build].memory` needs raising, and a build that dies
without explanation on a small runner is usually this.

## 4. Cross-compilation

⛔ **native-image does not cross-compile.** It builds for the machine it runs
on.

⭐ **The only route is a container for the target architecture**, natively where
a runner exists and under emulation otherwise. ⚠ Emulated native-image builds
are extremely slow, plausibly hours; treat aarch64 as needing a native runner.

## 5. CPU features

```sh
native-image -march=compatibility ...   # ⭐ the portable choice
native-image -march=native ...          # ⛔ never for distribution
```

⚠ **native-image's default `-march` has changed between versions** and has
defaulted to something above baseline. ⛔ **Set `-march=compatibility`
explicitly** rather than relying on the default.

## 6. External libraries

JNI libraries are `dlopen`ed and ⛔ do not work in a static image unless
statically linked in, which needs per-library work.

⚠ **Reflection, dynamic proxies, resource loading and service loaders are the
real constraint**, not native libraries. native-image performs closed-world
analysis: anything reached only reflectively is not in the image.

⭐ **The answer is reachability metadata**: `reflect-config.json`,
`resource-config.json` and friends, generated by the tracing agent:

```sh
java -agentlib:native-image-agent=config-output-dir=meta -jar app.jar
```

⛔ **The agent only records what the run exercised.** A code path not taken
during tracing is missing from the image, and it fails at run time with a
`ClassNotFoundException` in production. Tracing must cover the program's real
usage, and this is the second big trap.

## 7. TLS and certificates

⭐ **`--enable-url-protocols=https` is needed**, and the truststore must be
handled:

| option | trade |
| --- | --- |
| ⛔ build-time truststore, the default | frozen at build time, like `webpki-roots` |
| ⭐ `-H:+RuntimeCertificateHandling`, or setting `javax.net.ssl.trustStore` at run time | reads the host's store |

## 8. DNS

⚠ **`--enable-all-security-services` and the JDK's resolver.** A static image
uses the JDK's own resolution paths, which read `/etc/resolv.conf`. ⚠ NSS is
not consulted.

## 9. Locale

⛔ **native-image includes only the default locale unless told otherwise:**

```sh
native-image -H:+IncludeAllLocales ...        # large
native-image -H:IncludeLocales=en,de,fr ...   # ⭐ preferred
```

⚠ **A program that formats dates for a user's locale and was built without
this silently formats them wrongly.** This is a real and easy-to-miss defect.

## 10. Plugins

⛔ Class loading at run time does not work in a closed-world image. A plugin
architecture is incompatible with native-image.

## 11. Kernel

**documented**: inherits the libc floor.

## 12. Reproducibility

⚠ **Weak, and honestly so.**

| control | |
| --- | --- |
| ⭐ dependencies | Gradle or Maven lockfiles; ⛔ `--refresh-dependencies` must not be used |
| build path | ⚠ native-image has no documented path-remapping flag; rely on the fixed `/build` |
| ⛔ the image build itself | ⚠ has been reported as not bit-reproducible across runs; **not verified here** |

⛔ **Treat JVM native images as `unverified` for reproducibility** until a
project demonstrates otherwise on its own code. Recorded in
[`../../open-questions.md`](../../open-questions.md).

## 13. Debugging and size

`-g` produces DWARF. ⚠ Images are large: 20 MB to 80 MB is ordinary, because
the image contains the parts of the JDK the program reaches.

`--gc=serial` and `-Os` reduce it. `-H:+StripDebugInfo` after.

## 14. ⭐ Production defaults, failure modes, when not to

**Defaults**

```toml
[build]
image  = "ghcr.io/graalvm/native-image-community@sha256:..."
memory = "8G"
deps   = ["musl-dev", "zlib-static", "build-base"]

[build.script]
run = """
./gradlew --offline nativeCompile \
  -Pnative.args="--static --libc=musl --no-fallback -march=compatibility \
                 -H:IncludeLocales=en"
"""

[verify]
run = ["--version"]
```

**Failure modes**

| symptom | cause |
| --- | --- |
| ⛔ the binary needs a JVM at run time | ⭐ a fallback image; `--no-fallback` was omitted |
| `ClassNotFoundException` in production only | reflection metadata incomplete; the tracing run missed a path |
| ⛔ `SIGILL` on older hardware | the default `-march`; set `compatibility` |
| dates or numbers formatted wrongly | locales not included |
| the build dies with no message | out of memory; raise `[build].memory` |
| the image is 60 MB | ⚠ expected |

**⛔ When not to**: the program loads classes at run time; reflection cannot be
enumerated; the build cannot be done natively for every target architecture.

---

## 15. The alternative: ship a JVM

⭐ **Often the better answer**, and it should be considered before native-image.

```sh
jlink --add-modules "$(jdeps --print-module-deps app.jar)" \
      --strip-debug --no-header-files --no-man-pages --compress=2 \
      --output out/runtime
jpackage --type app-image --runtime-image out/runtime --main-jar app.jar
```

| | native-image | jlink runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| size | 20 to 80 MB | ⚠ 40 to 100 MB |
| startup | ⭐ milliseconds | ⚠ hundreds of milliseconds |
| ⛔ reflection | must be enumerated | ⭐ works normally |
| ⛔ plugins | impossible | ⭐ work normally |
| build complexity | ⚠ high | ⭐ low |
| static | ⭐ yes | ⚠ the JVM itself is dynamically linked |

⚠ **A jlink runtime is not a static binary.** It is a self-contained directory
that still needs a host libc. It is `portable = false` in this system's terms
and it is honest about what it is, which is better than a fallback image
pretending to be static.
